node_fixture.name: p8test_dhcp_primary
header: # MOCK-APPLY node fixture `p8test_dhcp_primary` (HQ 2026-10-27 ruling 7) for openvpn_server (and network_vpn). Production's
# VPN gateways hand the class their primary interface (network_dhcp iface = $::networking['primary'] = openvpn_server's
# $local_interface): the class rewrites /etc/network/interfaces for it, for lo:0 and for the bridge br0, and restarts
# ifupdown networking. The lab node's real NICs are never handed over (fixture rule), so this supplies a stand-in
# primary interface: p8test0, one end of a veth pair whose other end lives in the network namespace p8testdhcp, where
# dnsmasq answers DHCP with the single address 203.0.113.50 and no router option (the node's default route and DNS stay
# on NIC1, its SSH path on NIC2). The class then manages p8test0 exactly as production manages the primary interface.
# Behaviour of a real uplink (clients reaching the server over the primary interface) is NOT verified by a GREEN with it.
# Lifted by: a node whose primary interface the class may take over (a disposable gateway VM; no nodes.yml kind yet)
resources: exec[p8test stand-in primary interface p8test0 with a DHCP server in netns p8testdhcp]
node_fixture.scope_evidence: p8test_dhcp_primary: package[dnsmasq-base] supplies the dnsmasq binary for the stand-in DHCP server; exec[p8test stand-in primary interface p8test0 ...] (guarded unless 'ip link show p8test0') creates veth p8test0/p8test0p, moves the peer into netns p8testdhcp and runs dnsmasq there serving only 203.0.113.50 with empty router (3) and DNS (6) options, so the node's default route/DNS (NIC1) and SSH path (NIC2) are untouched; its only link to the class is 'before => Class[network_dhcp]' (ordering), it declares or alters no resource of openvpn_server or network_dhcp; within the stated stand-in scope
